title: METOC Analyst Forecaster (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I
raw_text:
2.     MOS 6842, METOC Analyst Forecaster (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I

    a. Summary. Typical duties of the METOC Analyst Forecaster include
observing, collecting, recording, validating, processing, disseminating, and
assimilation of METOC data and information to formulate forecasts and
environmental assessments. METOC Analyst Forecasters use and perform
preventive maintenance on METOC sensors, information technology systems, and
equipment.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must possess an EL score of 105 or GT score of 105 or higher.

        (3) Must have 36 months obligated service remaining upon graduation
from the MOS producing school.

            (4) Security requirement:

            (a) Must meet sensitive compartmented information (SCI)
eligibility guidelines based on a single scope background investigation/T5
investigation.

            (b) Prior to conducting the lateral move interview, all
applicants must complete a screening with a special security officer (SSO) to
determine TS/SCI eligibility.

            (5) Lateral move:

            (a) METOC OJT of 90 days is recommended for lateral move Marines
before attending the 6842 MOS school.

            (b) Marines must be a corporal through sergeant of any MOS and
must be approved by the METOC OccFld specialist.

            (c) Marines who execute a lateral move to the 6842 MOS must
attend PMOS training within six (6) months of reporting to a command offering
on-the-job training (OJT).

            (d) The 6842 MOS is eligible for prior meteorological service
members with less than 10 years TIS and on a limited-if-necessary-basis, for


                                          3-436                        Enclosure (1)
 3145                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L



inter-service transfers of previously qualified and certified meteorology
forecasters with less than 10 years TIS, as determined and approved by MMEA
and the METOC OccFld specialist.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Meteorological and Oceanographic Analyst Forecaster
Course (ITRO Phase 1) (F02WAK1) at MARDET Keesler AFB, MS.

        (2) Complete the Marine Corps Meteorological Oceanographer Analyst
Forecaster Course (Phase 2) (F02WAM2) at MARDET Keesler AFB, MS.

    d. Duties. For a complete list of duties and tasks, refer to MCRP 2-
10B.6, MAGTF Meteorological and Oceanographic Operations and NAVMC 3500.38,
Meteorological and Oceanographic Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Atmospheric and Space Scientists 19-2021.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

The Meteorological and Oceanographic (METOC) Services OccFld is responsible for collecting, assessing, and disseminating environmental data, information, and intelligence, relevant to friendly and enemy force strengths and vulnerabilities for the planning and execution of operations necessary to characterize the battle space. This includes atmospheric, space, climatic, hydrologic, and littoral oceanographic information for use in the production of Tactical Decision Aids (TDA) and METOC effects matrices. The METOC OccFld is comprised of 6842 METOC Analyst Forecaster, 6891 METOC Chief, and 6802 METOC Services Officer. Marines entering the 6800 OccFld will complete formal training and receive MOS 6842. As their skill enhancing training progresses, they become eligible to attend MOSs 6852, 6862, and 6877 instruction.

matches: Gather data from sources such as surface or upper air stations, satellites, weather bureaus, or radar for use in meteorological reports or forecasts.

The Meteorological and Oceanographic (METOC) Services OccFld is responsible for collecting, assessing, and disseminating environmental data, information, and intelligence, relevant to friendly and enemy force strengths and vulnerabilities for the planning and execution of operations necessary to characterize the battle space.
Compile and evaluate hydrologic information to prepare navigational charts and maps and to predict atmospheric conditions.
This includes atmospheric, space, climatic, hydrologic, and littoral oceanographic information for use in the production of Tactical Decision Aids (TDA) and METOC effects matrices.

Collect, synthesize, analyze, manage, and report environmental data, such as pollution emission measurements, atmospheric monitoring measurements, meteorological or mineralogical information, or soil or water samples.

Typical duties of the METOC Analyst Forecaster include observing, collecting, recording, validating, processing, disseminating, and assimilation of METOC data and information to formulate forecasts and environmental assessments.
Observe work and monitor gauges, dials, and other indicators to ensure that operators conform to production or processing standards.
METOC Analyst Forecasters use and perform preventive maintenance on METOC sensors, information technology systems, and equipment.
Complete and maintain records of weather and beach conditions, emergency medical treatments performed, and other relevant incident information.
For a complete list of duties and tasks, refer to MCRP 2- 10B.6, MAGTF Meteorological and Oceanographic Operations and NAVMC 3500.38, Meteorological and Oceanographic Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
